News.title: Oil prices ‘could hit $150’ if US blocks Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
Oil could rise to $150 a barrel under a US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a major trader has warned.

Brent crude jumped to $102 on Monday after Donald Trump said he would cut off the crucial trade route, following the collapse of peace talks with Iran.

But Jorge Montepeque, managing director at Onyx Capital Group, said crude’s current level was “not reflective at all” of how far prices could spike.

Oil prices “should be $140, $150” if the naval blockade goes ahead, Mr Montepeque told Bloomberg. It is scheduled to begin at 3pm BST, according to US Central Command.

Mr Trump said the move would stop “any and all ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz”. US Central Command later said the blockade would apply to ships “entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas”.

A blockade of Iran would cut off around 4pc of global oil production. Oil has already leapt from around $60 per barrel before the war after Iran closed Hormuz to trade traffic. The waterway carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies.

News.title: Free-range chickens let outside after six-month bird flu poultry ‘flockdown’
News.content:
Farmed birds in England have been let outside after being cooped up for six months in a bird flu lockdown, it has been announced.

The mandatory housing order, introduced by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) in late October, required all poultry birds in England and Wales to be kept indoors in barns and coops around the clock.

The housing order, which was finally lifted on April 9, meant that even birds sold as ‘free-range’ were prevented from going outdoors at any time to minimise their contact with wild birds which carry and spread avian flu.

The regulations applied to flocks of 50 or more birds and to any sellers of poultry products like meat and eggs.

The scale of H5N1 bird flu outbreaks on poultry farms in the UK, Europe, and the US since 2020 has been described as unprecedented, with more than five million birds culled in Britain alone over the last four years.

If even a single case is detected on a farm, farmers are legally required to slaughter the entire flock to stamp the virus out quickly.

Bird flu cases typically peak in the winter months, when many wild birds migrate south and spread the virus through their faeces and saliva.

“With the threat of avian influenza receding, birds can now be allowed access to ranges and outdoor areas,” said deputy UK chief veterinary officer Jorge Martin-Alamagro.

“Although the risk to poultry has reduced, there remains a risk that poultry and other captive birds can still contract bird flu. It is still essential that bird keepers remain vigilant and implement rigorous and strict biosecurity,” he added.

News.title: Eastern Equine Encephalitis
News.content:
Key facts

Eastern equine encephalitis (EEE) is a rare but serious disease

The virus is spread through the bites of infected mosquitoes

Approximately 30 per cent of those who develop severe cases will die

There is no vaccine or specific medicine

The best way to avoid the disease is to not get bitten by mosquitoes.

Overview

EEE – also known as triple E – is a virus that affects the brain and nervous system. It is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito. However, it is rare, with an average of just 11 cases reported every year.

The virus primarily resides in birds and rodents, mainly on the Atlantic and Gulf coast of the United States. But it has also been found in Central and Latin America, Canada, and the Caribbean.

Signs and symptoms

Symptoms of EEE can include

Fever

Headaches

Vomiting and diarrhoea

Seizures

Behavioural changes

Drowsiness

The infection can progress to encephalitis, which is an inflammation of the brain. Meningitis, an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, may also occur. Some people may be infected without showing any symptoms, though data is limited.

Dangers and complications

EEE is a very serious disease with a high fatality rate of around 30 per cent. Many survivors of EEE experience ongoing neurological problems and can be left with lifelong mental and physical disabilities due to the damage caused to the brain and central nervous system. The effects can range from behavioural changes and memory loss to paralysis and permanent brain damage.

Transmission

The EEE virus cycles between the Culiseta melanura mosquito and birds. Mosquitoes become carriers after feeding on infected birds or rodents, and then transmit the virus to humans and other animals. The virus cannot be spread directly between humans, and humans and horses do not circulate enough of the virus in their bodies to pass it back to mosquitoes.

The disease is most prevalent in freshwater swamps in the Gulf and Atlantic states of the US. People working outdoors in these areas are most at risk of the disease.

Treatment

Currently, there are no specific medicines or vaccines for EEE. Treatment mainly focuses on hospitalisation and pain management. Patients with severe symptoms may need pain control for headaches and anti-sickness therapy and rehydration. Patients with encephalitis – inflammation of the brain – will need close monitoring.

Prevention

Prevention is crucial due to the lack of available treatments. Avoiding mosquito bites is the best way to prevent contracting the virus. People in affected areas are advised to wear long sleeves and trousers and apply insect repellent. Use screens on doors and windows and drain standing water from items like buckets and plant pots.

History

EEE was first detected in horses in the 1830s. The US records an average of 11 human cases of EEE each year. The largest recorded outbreak occurred in 2019, with 38 cases and six deaths in Massachusetts.

Useful links

cdc.gov/eastern-equine-encephalitis

mass.gov/eee-eastern-equine-encephalitis

www.woah.org/equine-encephalomyelitis-eastern/

Sports.title: Joe Cole demands investigation into how Chelsea let ‘future captain’ leave for just £18million
Sports.content:
JOE COLE has questioned how Marc Guehi was allowed to leave Chelsea after he netted in Man City’s 3-0 romp at Stamford Bridge.

Guehi produced a fine finish against his boyhood club for City’s second goal of the game as he helped them secure a huge result in the title race.





The England defender joined the Blues aged six but struggled to get in the first team and was sold to Crystal Palace for £18million in 2021.

He turned into a top player at Selhurst Park and was even linked with a return to Chelsea before City snapped him up for around £20m in January.

Chelsea have lacked a top quality centre back in recent years and club legend Cole is amazed the Blues let Gueho leave.

He demanded an inquest into who allowed Guehi to depart given the club are lacking quality in their backline.

Cole told The Dressing Room Podcast: “I’m looking at him and I’m thinking: how has this kid got a Manchester City shirt on? The team should have been built around him five years ago.

“Whoever has let him out the door at Chelsea… if I’m the owner, I’m going, ‘Right, who’s decision, or what collective of people’s decision, was it to think it was a good idea to let this kid leave the club?’.

“Everyone would go, ‘It wasn’t me, it wasn’t me!’… unless you find out who is making these decisions, these decisions will continue to happen and you’ll keep losing players like that. You need to do an appraisal on it.”

Cole, who played 282 times for Chelsea, winning three Premier League titles and another three domestic cups, said Guehi outlined how important a player he is during City’s win.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He added: “For me, the big moment in the game from a Chelsea perspective, and from a Manchester City perspective, was when Marc Guehi scored the goal.

“It was a great finish but I look at where Chelsea are as a club, desperately trying to find a centre-half, spending hundreds of millions of pounds… you had a kid [Guehi] in the building.

“He came over and spoke to us and he’s so assured, he’s a captain. You see him play and he’s calm.

“He came from Chelsea from the age of six, we sold him to Crystal Palace and now he’s at Manchester City and he looks like he’s been there for 20 years.”



Guehi paid tribute to Chelsea after the game and admitted he “wouldn’t be here without this football club”.

He added: “I am eternally grateful to every single member of the staff who helped me in the academy and the club for picking me up at such a young age, to Frank Lampard and Jody Morris for giving me my debut when I was here.

“It’s nice to be back.”

Guehi has also become a first choice centre-back for England after picking up 27 caps and he is expected to start at this summer’s World Cup.

Sports.content:
JUSTICE FOR LEGEND Maradona ‘house of horrors’ death retrial begins a year after court case dramatically collapsed over glam judge’s TV doc

A NEW trial over the death of Argentine football icon Diego Maradona will begin after he died in a ‘house of horrors’ while allegedly being treated like an animal.

The fresh court probe comes nearly a year after a previous case collapsed into a mistrial where one of the judges was forced to resign following a TV appearance.





Seven members of the legend’s medical team were charged with negligent homicide after he tragically died from a heart attack at just 60 years old.

Maradona had been recovering from a brain surgery to remove a blood clot at the time of his death in 2020.

The defendants include psychiatrist Agustina Cosachov, neurosurgeon Leopoldo Luque, psychologist Carlos Angel Diaz, physician Nancy Edith Forlini, nurse Ricardo Almiron, head nurse Mariano Ariel Perroni, and physician Pedro Pablo Di Spagna.



On Tuesday, they will face a court on San Isidro, near Buenos Aires, where nearly 100 witnesses will give evidence over the death of the 1986 World Cup champion.

An eighth defendant – nurse Dahiana Madrid – will face court in a separate jury trial at a later date.

All eight co-accused have denied wrongdoing.

Last May, a mistrial was declared when it was revealed that judge Julieta Makintach had been interviewed by a camera crew two months into the case in the corridors of the courthouse and in her office.



The bombshell interviews had been part of a documentary.

Dubbed the “judge of God”, she featured in a trailer for the six-part mini-series which was embarrassingly played to the court.

Her involvement in the show was in breach of the judicial rules and she was forced to resign.

The five-month trial exposed chilling claims about the footballer’s death which included being treated like an animal by the medical team.

The retrial has required both sides of the tense legal battle to reassess their courtroom strategies as the first trial aired photographs, videos, audio recordings and forensic evidence.



Multiple witnesses, including Maradona’s children and his former wife, Claudia Villafane, have already given evidence to the court.

Previously, prosecutors argued that the medical team had broken treatment protocols, labelling the home where Maradona was recovering a “theatre of horror“.

They also alleged that necessary care had not been provided to the football great.

Autopsy expert Mauricio Cassinelli told a court the champion had “a heart that weighed more than twice its normal size.”



He died in a dark room lying in agony for half a day before suffering a heart attack.

The star experienced dilated cardiomyopathy, a disease of the heart muscle that caused his heart chambers to enlarge and stretch.

He also suffered from cirrhosis which damaged his liver, as well as myocarditis which occurs when the heart becomes inflamed.



Allegations include Maradona being allowed to drink beer in the morning and was later given sleeping pills dissolved in his booze at night, all while under the accused’s medical care.

It has also been alleged that he was washed down with a hosepipe rather than being helped to the shower.

Chief prosecutor Patricio Ferrari shocked the room, holding up a bleak picture of the player’s last day, which showed the Argentinian icon lying on his back with his bloated stomach exposed under a lifted-up black T-shirt.

“This is the way he died,” Ferrari told the court.

“In that House of Horror where Diego Maradona died no one did what they had to do,” Ferrari added.



But the defence hit back, saying his death had been inevitable due to his existing health issues.

Off the pitch, Maradona struggled for decades with cocaine and alcohol addiction, tarnishing his illustrious career.

The negligence charges were laid in 2021 when prosecutors appointed a medical board to investigate his death.

The panel of experts concluded that the star’s medical team acted in an “inappropriate, deficient and reckless” manner.

If convicted, the group of defendants could face between eight and 25 years behind bars.



The enduring presence in Argentina – still depicted in towering murals to tattoos – was found dead in a rented home in Tigre, painting a tragic picture of the star’s fall from grace in his grim final days.

Maradona – born in 1960 – was widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He led Argentina to World Cup glory in 1986, famously scoring the “Hand of God” goal and the “Goal of the Century” against England.

His incredible dribbling, vision, and flair made him a global icon, inspiring generations of footballers, including Lionel Messi.

Sports.title: Popular American tradition banned for World Cup causing fan outrage
Sports.content:
TAILGATING outside Gillette Stadium has been banned ahead of the World Cup – leaving fans furious.

The home of the New England Patriots and New England Revolution will host seven showdowns during the iconic tournament between June 13 and July 9.





But it has been confirmed that tailgating will not be allowed outside Gillette Stadium, which will be known as Boston Stadium for sponsorship reasons during the World Cup.

Match-going fans have also been warned they will be breaking the law if they possess or drink alcohol in public areas.

Guidelines on the Boston Host Committee for the Fifa World Cup’s website read: “Please note that the traditional ‘tailgating’ (eating and drinking around parked cars) is not permitted for these events.

“In Massachusetts, it is illegal to possess or drink from open containers of alcohol in public spaces.”

READ MORE ON WORLD CUP NEW LOOK MetLife Stadium officially renamed for 2026 World Cup with signs covered up

And the announcement has sparked outrage among fans – with some racing onto social media to vent their fury over the popular American tradition being prohibited.

One said: “Why even host the games??? It defeats the entire purpose for tourists to truly get a full experience for the World Cup honestly.”

Another added: “Pay an arm and a leg to get there and can’t have any fun.”

A third chimed in: “Why hold the World Cup in the USA if you’re not going to allow us to tailgate?”



A fourth bluntly noted: “Shambles.”

Parking around the stadium will also be drastically reduced from the usual 20,000 spots to 5,000 for the World Cup.

Organizers insist a larger safety perimeter is needed, while hospitality events will require additional space.



Fans are instead being pushed to use public transport – with the MBTA charging $80 for round-trip train tickets between Boston’s South Station and Foxboro Station.

MetLife Stadium, which will be referred to as New Jersey New York Stadium during the tournament, has also banned tailgating and is offering no parking.

Scotland, Haiti, Norway, Iraq, Morocco, England, Ghana and France are all set to head to Boston for group stage clashes.

A last 32 showdown will also be held at the 65,878-capacity stadium, along with a quarter-final on July 9.

Sports.title: Liverpool make major stadium change before PSG clash after star suffered horror injury
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have made changes to their advertising hoardings ahead of their clash against PSG after Galatasaray star Noa Lang suffered a serious injury last month.

The Dutchman crashed into the hoardings during his side’s 4-0 defeat to the Reds on March 18.





The 26-year-old lacerated his right thumb and was seriously hurt as he was taken off on a stretcher.

Lang – who had only entered the action as a substitute – was subbed off in the 80th minute and replaced by Mauro Icardi.

He underwent emergency surgery after the freak accident that saw him nearly lose his thumb.

Liverpool and Uefa had launched an investigation into the incident and how Lang’s thumb became stuck in the middle of two panels.

And according to the Athletic, Liverpool have now modified their advertising hoardings close to the goals that have a gap.

Uefa is said to be “reviewing the pitchside set-up, including LED boards at all upcoming matches, to identify any potential comparable risks and ask clubs to take appropriate measures if necessary”.

Liverpool are reportedly confident Lang’s issue was a freak accident that will not happen again after their changes.

Arne Slot’s men welcome PSG to Anfield on Tuesday night bidding to overturn a 2-0 deficit from the first leg.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

SunSport has reached out to Uefa for comment.

Lang was still able to go on international duty with Holland despite his injury as he revealed the impact it was having on his life.

On his injury, Lang said: “My thumb is still intact. It might be possible to stitch it back together.

“The doctor expects the finger to survive. At the moment, I can’t play on the PlayStation.



“I’m right-handed, so this isn’t a minor issue when I go to the toilet. I also need help getting into the shower.”

Lang explained that he was hoping to use the hoardings to cushion his fall during the Liverpool game but said they were “sharper” than he thought.

He continued: “I wanted to cushion the blow with the advertising hoardings, but they turned out to be rather sharp. The tip of my thumb was dangling.”

Lang had previously written from hospital: “S*** happens. Surgery went well! Thanks for all the messages.”

And Gala general secretary Eray Yazga said: “We made a complaint to Uefa representatives after the match.

“They also made their investigations. Uefa will evaluate the issue. We are in talks with lawyers.

“We will file a lawsuit for compensation to Uefa. We will ask for our victimisation in terms of salary to be eliminated.”

Sports.title: Gary Neville’s brutal one-word response to Mark Goldbridge question comes back to haunt him after buying YouTube channel
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE’S X post in which he rejected Mark Goldbridge coming on The Overlap has resurfaced.

It comes after Neville‘s The Overlap bought Goldbridge’s two YouTube channels.





The media company owned by Neville announced the news of the investment on Tuesday.

Goldbridge’s “That’s Football” and “The United Stand” were bought for a reported seven-figure-fee.

And since the purchase, fans have dug out an old post by Neville on X.

Three years ago one fan wrote: “Will Mark Goldbridge ever get invited onto The Overlap? The guy has the biggest MUFC fan channel and has a lot of football knowledge. It would be great to see him be brought on.”

The United legend and Sky Sports pundit, who founded The Overlap, swiftly shut down the question with an abrupt “no”.

So three years later after buying Goldbridge’s channels, Neville might have had a change of heart.

Goldbridge will continue to front both channels, which have a combined 3.7million subscribers.

However, they are set to be expanded as part of the takeover.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The United Stand will be expanded to include “Stick to United” as part of the “Stick to Football” podcast brand.

Journalists and former Man Utd players are expected to feature on the new show.

A new United news show named “The Daily United” will also be introduced.

Following the purchase Neville said: “We are building what we believe will become one of the most exciting independent football communities in the world – one that gives fans direct, personality-led content.



“The United Stand and That’s Football are two of the best-known football channels on YouTube, and our intention is to develop them into the most compelling Manchester United and football news channels in the market.”

Goldbridge added: “I’ve spent the last 10 years building The United Stand for Manchester United fans and That’s Football for all fans, and I’m prouder of that than anything I’ve ever done. This deal is about what comes next.

“The Overlap has the ambition, the credibility, and the resources to help me take what I do to the next level.”

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Blues face fresh fine, protesting fans’ damning blast at owners and Defoe’s scouting mission
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S defeat by Manchester City has added fuel to the fire of Saturday’s fan protest ahead of the Manchester United game.

The NotAProjectCFC group will lead the march with a simple message: BlueCo Out.





David and Jacob, leading figures at NAPCFC, told SunSport why the 3-0 beating by City was such a damning indictment of the Blues’ owners and their recruitment philosophy.

Former Chelsea Academy player Marc Guehi scored the second goal, after moving to the Etihad in January along with winger Antoine Semenyo.

Jacob said: “I think we can talk at length about how the club operate, but it was men against boys on Sunday.

“I think it was quite ironic that Marc Guehi scored a lovely goal at the Bridge and celebrated like it meant something big to him.

“That was a bit of a slap in the face.

“Can you imagine what Marc Guehi or Antoine Semenyo would probably have done to our team in January if the club had been prepared to put their hand in their pocket and pay people comparable salaries, rather than try and bring young talent in and lowball them and hope that they stay?”

Jacob and David discussed a number of issues, including Liam Rosenior’s appointment, which you can watch on YouTube.

The crux of their anger, though, is not merely Chelsea’s recruitment – it is the model as a whole.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They believe the identity of their club is being torn away from them, a feeling shared by some Strasbourg fans.

Supporters from BlueCo’s French club will join Saturday’s protest.

David added: “I think we are at a point now where we do not have any faith that this current ownership are the right people to take the club forward.

“When we first set up as a protest group around the turn of the year, just a few days before Enzo Maresca left the club,

“I think there was a feeling that we felt that with enough media pressure, we could perhaps put enough spotlight on the project itself and maybe look at a change to the model.



“Based on our communications with the club since, and based on our communications with people who probably better understand finances than we do, it doesn’t look like a realistic possibility.”

The last protest NAPCFC organised, ahead of the game against Brentford in January, was less impactful than they would have liked.

But it was still covered by plenty of media outlets, and it did prompt Chelsea director Danny Finkelstein to contact the group to arrange a meeting.

NAPCFC later revealed details of the encounter, including the claim Finkelstein told them it was “f***ing obvious” the Blues were building one of the best teams in the world.

Jacob and David feel they have planned much better and think Saturday’s event has the potential to be a huge turning point in Chelsea’s history.



David said: “For us the Brentford protest was a good way for us to work out how to structure these things going forward.

“The club reached out to the group, and we had everything that came from that.

“So there’s no doubt for us that it’s been part of something. But it’s about taking it on to the next level on Saturday.

“I think we’re approaching a point now where either you’re on one side or the other.

“It’s getting to the serious point of, if you do oppose protests, then you enable what Clearlake are doing and ripping the soul out of the club, and BlueCo ripping the soul out of the club, I should say.



“So this is an important moment. I think the image of us standing alongside Strasbourg will be powerful regardless of the overall number that are behind us.”

Jacob added: “David and I are not guys that are regularly out there on the picket line somewhere.

“It was something that we got involved in accidentally, and because we are passionate fans.

“I want my children to feel the same way about my football club as I did growing up. It was everything to me.



“These last four years have been really challenging from a football perspective.

“I should probably learn to detach the emotion from it, but it’s very difficult when you’ve loved the club for 30+ years, and been going to the stadium and having such nostalgic feelings.

“I don’t believe under this ownership, if we continue with this ownership, that we will have a football club that is representative of that.

“I’m not telling everyone, ‘this is our view, and it’s the right view.’ We believe that these aren’t the right people for the club. We want to do something about it.

“I think it’s evident with what we’ve seen over the last four years, and in particular, more recently, with the continuous churn of managers.



“They continuously try to control narratives…but there is no reality to it.

“I think it’s obvious that it is not working and that they do not have the best intentions for our football club. Look at the financial reports that have just come out.”

The protest will take place on Saturday, starting at the Wolfpack Inn at 6.30pm. Fans will march to Stamford Bridge for roughly 15 minutes ahead of the game against Manchester United.

SunSport will bring you complete coverage of that on our social media platforms and website.

FRIEND OR DEFOE?



Chelsea U21’s were defeated by Fulham in the final matchday of the Premier League 2 season, but still lifted the title.

At the game, though, was a familiar face for any Premier League fan – Jermain Defoe.

Defoe, now the manager of Woking FC, sat with the media and scouts at Fulham’s Motspur Park.

The former England striker would have been impressed by Shim Mheuka, who scored again for the young Blues, bringing his season total to 24 goals across all competitions

Mheuka will be out of reach for Woking.



But the young centre forward will be keen on a loan next season if he is unable to force his way into Chelsea’s first-team squad on a regular basis.

DISSENT DISASTER

Chelsea have received more yellow cards for dissent than any other team in the Premier League.

Perhaps a sign of the overall frustrations at Stamford Bridge, or the level of immaturity within the squad.



Chelsea have received 16 yellow cards for dissent in the Premier League, with both Estevao and Marc Cucurella receiving one each in Sunday’s defeat to Man City.

Vice-captain Enzo Fernandez has received four alone, more than any other player in the squad.

The Blues are achieving all this even without Nicolas Jackson, who is currently on loan at Bayern Munich.

Jackson infamously earned 10 bookings in his first season at the club, only one of them for a foul.

Yet the Senegal striker has received one yellow and one red card in 27 appearances for Bayern, while recording eight goals and four assists.



Jackson’s replacement, Liam Delap, has been booked twice and sent off once – for two yellow cards in seven minutes in the Carabao Cup tie at Wolves back in October.

Delap has two goals and four assists in his 34 appearances for the Blues.

FINE TIME

The Blues are facing yet another fine from the authorities.



The amount is trivial but the surrounding issues are not.

Chelsea Football Club Women Limited should have filed accounts for last season by the end of March at Companies House.

The financial penalty for a private company is £150 for being up to a month late, rising gradually to a maximum of £1,500 for over six months.

It is a bit of a mystery why full figures for the women’s team were not part of the information dump filed at CH earlier this week.

Owners BlueCo published their own results as well as those of the men’s team and other associated companies.



Within the BlueCo 22 Limited accounts, it was revealed CFC Women lost £17.1m in 2024-25 (up from £8.4m), despite turnover increasing by £9.8m as Sonia Bompastor’s side claimed a domestic Treble.

Eagle-eyed observers noticed something interesting in the figures for Chelsea FC Holdings, however.

The parent company of the men’s team received £22.6m from Chelsea Women last season – which was more than the women’s team’s total income of £21.3m.

It is believed the £22.6m includes the proceeds of selling the Kingsmeadow stadium to the women’s team.

And it also represents some kind of licensing agreement which allows the women’s team to exploit the Chelsea name and brand, as well as to benefit from services and facilities like Stamford Bridge that are controlled by Chelsea FC Holdings.



The latter’s accounts also revealed the company PAID out £11.3m to Chelsea Women over the course of last season.

But we won’t know for sure what the payments in either direction were for until the women’s team file their full figures at Companies House.

They will make interesting reading, not least for Aston Villa.

The owners of Villa have followed BlueCo in effectively selling their women’s team to themselves as a means of keeping the men’s team on the right side of the Premier League’s Profit and Sustainability Rules.

Chelsea would have breached PSR without the £198.7m profit from the sale of the women’s team in 2023-24.



SunSport understand the PL were aware of the Blues’ intention to charge the women’s team a licensing fee going forward.

And there has been no indication yet the PL is disputing the value of that agreement.

So expect Villa to follow their lead.

COMM OFF IT



Chelsea are sensitive about reporting of the increase in the executive wage bill last season.

And so they should be.

As SunSport revealed, the total cost of senior executives rose by nearly 80 per cent to £10.6m last season, despite the club making Premier League-record losses of £262.4m.

The club are at pains to point out the much bigger total was down to a significant increase in the number of staff classed as “key management personnel”, not huge pay rises for those who were already in that category.

But fans are still entitled to ask whether the Stamford Bridge suits who received £4.7m more between them last year are earning their keep.



Take the commercial department, for instance.

The Chelsea FC Holdings accounts revealed a fall in commercial income last season from £225.3m in the prior year to £200.9m, “largely due to reduced sponsorship revenue”.

In the summer, chief revenue officer Casper Stylsvig left the club after rows about the failure to find a new long-term front-of-shirt sponsor willing to meet the Blues’ valuation.

For the third season in a row, Chelsea began this campaign without such a deal, following the expiry of the agreement with mobile phone company 3 at the end of 2022-23 season.

Former Tottenham suit Todd Kline was promoted to president of commercial and in February the Blues announced a deal until the end of the season with Swedish AI firm IFS.



But not for the first time this season, claims there would soon be more good news on that front are are yet to be fulfilled.

And if Liam Rosenior’s team fail to qualify for the Champions League, the value of the shirt sponsorship and other deals will fall.

Chelsea ARE predicting club record revenues of around £700m this season.

But a lot of that increase will come from qualification for the Champions League and prize money from the Club World Cup – which were earned by the players, not the executives.

And there is still the issue of the progress – or lack of it – on a new stadium.



Building a modern, 60,000-seater ground is the single most important off-field task Chelsea chiefs face. Getting it right is probably the only way the current owners can increase the value of the asset on which they have already spent £4billion.

Yet nearly four years after the Clearlake Capital/Todd Boehly takeover, the club appears no nearer to resolving the problem.

WELCOME TO THE CHEAP SEATS

Chelsea’s clash with Manchester City last Sunday felt like a massive game that rich fans would love to watch.



But there were notably some empty seats in the West Stand opposite the press box.

And when you look at the prices the Blues are charging for Saturday’s big clash with Manchester United, you can see why.

At the time of going to press, there were still hospitality packages available in most categories.

They start at £595 plus VAT – in other words, more than £700 – for the right to see the game while paying for food and drink in areas away from the great unwashed.

And prices go right up to £7,495 plus VAT if you want to be in The Dugout Club.



For that, you get to greet the Chelsea team as they arrive, to watch the warm-up from the touchline, and to enjoy a post-match meet and greet with a player.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The package includes padded seats behind the home bench and swanky food and drink. Chelsea even throw in a matchday programme.

SunSport will have a think about it.

Sports.title: ‘There I was, crying’ – Liverpool icon left emotional in return to football as CEO of Malaysian club
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL legend Luis Garcia has admitted he was reduced to tears when his Malaysian club celebrated an historic win.

The former Spain midfielder retired from football in 2014 before a brief return to the game in 2016.





He has since worked as a pundit and didn’t think he would return to football.

But last summer he joined Malaysian side Johor Darul Ta’zim as their chief executive.

And Garcia has revealed he was left emotional after the team reached the quarter-finals of the Asian Champions League for the first team.

The club overcame Sanfrecce Hiroshima 3-2 on aggregate and will face Al-Ahli or Al-Duhail in the next round.

He told the Guardian: “I was always very competitive and once I had left football, I thought I wasn’t going to have those feelings I had before.

“I still enjoy football, still play seven-a-side with my friends – every Saturday at 10am, Los Jareños Club de Futbol – but I thought I had lost that and it wasn’t coming back.

“In fact, I was trying to avoid it; I didn’t want it. So when it happened, it surprised me. I didn’t expect football to give me that again. But there I was, crying.

“When I saw them jumping with joy, having been with them every day, sharing the long journeys, from Malaysia to Vietnam and back, on to Japan, and then saw them win I got that emotion again.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Garcia started his playing career with Barcelona and also had a spell with Atletico Madrid.

He moved to Liverpool in 2004 and enjoyed a Champions League triumph in his first season.

Garcia started as the Reds secured a dramatic penalty shootout win over AC Milan after coming back from 3-0 down.

He went on to win the FA Cup and Super Cup with Liverpool and reached another Champions League final in 2006-07.



Garcia played 122 times for Liverpool and then left Anfield as a cult iconm in 2007 to return to Atletico.

He later had stints with Racing Santander before playing in Mexico and India.

Garcia said a move into coaching never interested him after his retirement.

He claimed he was more attracted to the business side of football because he didn’t want “pressure without being able to impact the game”.

Garcia said: “When I retired, I was relaxed, welcomed the pause, but I had also spent years getting ready for other opportunities that might arise in football.



“I did a master’s with Uefa, a sporting director’s course, my coaching badges. Any qualification that was on the table, I took it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But I didn’t want to coach. I always preferred the business side of it to the on-pitch stuff because I suffered a lot on the pitch.

“The idea of being a coach, being the other side of the line, all that pressure without being able to personally impact the game, didn’t appeal.”

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho deletes all Chelsea posts with pointed Man Utd message
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho deletes all Chelsea posts with pointed Man Utd message

Alejandro Garnacho has had a slow start to life with Chelsea following a £40m switch from Manchester United and has dropped a potential hint over what his future could potentially hold

View 2 Images Garnacho penned a seven-year deal with Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea star Alejandro Garnacho has deleted every reference to current side Chelsea on his TikTok after suggestions he could leave the club. The Argentine only joined the Blues in the summer after a £40m switch from Premier League rivals Manchester United.

‌



But Garnacho, 21, has had a difficult debut season at Stamford Bridge with just one Premier League goal to his name - albeit he has scored a further seven in other competitions.

‌



The former Atletico Madrid youngster signed a seven-year deal with Chelsea following his move from Old Trafford, but his social media activity appears to suggest he might not be planning to stay for that long.

‌



Garnacho has deleted every post from his official TikTok account referencing Chelsea, while the only ones left are from when he played for United. The winger also reshared a highlights compilation made by a fan during his time at Old Trafford.

Gary Neville identifies Man Utd detail that gives biggest hint yet over manager decision READ MORE :

Garnacho’s social media activity comes after he admitted that his exit from his former club ‘hurt’. Speaking to Premier League Productions, he said: “Maybe yes, because I loved that club.

‌



“They gave me the confidence from the start, from Spain, to bring me to the academy, then they bring me to the first team, so it was like four or five years, and amazing love from everyone, from the fans, the stadium, everything was really good.

“It's just sometimes you have to change for the good of your life or the next steps. I only have good memories of Man United.”

View 2 Images Garnacho joined Chelsea in the summer for £40m (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added: “I remember in the last six months I was just not playing like before at Manchester United. I started to be on the bench, it's not a bad thing, I was only 20 years old, but in my mind it was like I had to play every game.

“In my mind, maybe it is also on me, I started to do some bad things. But yes, it was just this moment in life and sometimes you have to make decisions and I am really proud to be here and still in the Premier League at a club like this.

“Everyone knows the team we have and the things we can do. Sometimes, we have better moments or worse moments, I am proud to be here but with United, I have nothing wrong to say about the club, no one in the club or the team-mates. It's just a moment in life that changes and life continues. I have no regrets.”

Sports.title: Birmingham star Marvin Ducksch charged with drink-driving after crash as club issue statement
Sports.content:
Birmingham star Marvin Ducksch charged with drink-driving after crash as club issue statement

Birmingham City attacker Marvin Ducksch has been charged with drink-driving following a three-vehicle collision on Easter Monday

View 2 Images Birmingham City striker Marvin Ducksch has been charged with drink-driving (Image: Kevin Hodgson/NurPhoto)

Birmingham City forward Marvin Ducksch has been charged with drink-driving following a three-vehicle crash on Easter Monday.

‌



Warwickshire Police were called to the incident on the A3400 near Henley-in-Arden, where the Blues' first-team training ground is located, at approximately 10:30pm and detained Ducksch at the scene. The two-time Germany international had earlier featured for Blues as a substitute in their 2-1 loss to Ipswich Town at Portman Road. Ducksch was formally charged by police on Monday, April 13.

‌



A statement from Warwickshire Police read: "A 32-year-old man from Solihull has been charged with drink driving following a collision near Henley-in-Arden.

‌



"At around 10.30pm on Monday, 6 April, officers attended a report of a three-vehicle collision on the A3400. Marvin Ducksch was arrested and was yesterday, 13 April, charged with drink driving.

View 2 Images Ducksch joined Blues from Werder Bremen last year (Image: Matt McNulty)

‌



"He has been bailed to appear before Warwickshire Magistrates in Leamington on Wednesday, 20 May."

Ducksch, who signed for Blues on a three-year deal from Werder Bremen last summer, was left out of the squad that beat Wrexham 2-0 on Sunday.

A club statement released on Tuesday read: "The club can confirm that Marvin Ducksch has been charged in relation to an offence of driving with excess alcohol.

"Marvin wishes to apologise to his teammates, staff and supporters of the club and accepts full responsibility for his actions. The matter has been dealt with internally and no further comment will be made at this time."

Sports.title: Liverpool make Anfield change for PSG Champions League tie after Noa Lang horror injury
Sports.content:
Liverpool make Anfield change for PSG Champions League tie after Noa Lang horror injury

Noa Lang was carried off on a stretcher after picking up a horrific finger injury during Galatasaray's defeat to Liverpool at Anfield last month

View 2 Images Liverpool officials inspect the fence against which Noa Lang sustained an injury (Image: (Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images))

Liverpool have altered the advertising hoardings at Anfield following Noa Lang’s serious thumb injury last month. The Galatasaray forward sustained a deep cut in a freak incident after crashing into the advertising hoarding as he chased a ball which went out of play during his side's 4-0 defeat.

‌



The Netherlands international received lengthy treatment, and some 45 minutes after the final whistle, he was taken out of the stadium still on a stretcher. Lang would go on to have emergency surgery at Whiston Hospital, and tonight is the first time the Reds have hosted a Champions League game since the incident as Arne Slot’s side take on Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Following the game, Liverpool and UEFA officials were spotted investigating the advertising hoarding where the incident occurred. And now, according to The Athletic, work has been carried out at Anfield to modify some of the boards around the goal areas which have an impact gap in the event of a player hitting them.

‌



However, the report also claims that while Liverpool believe what happened to Lang was a freak accident, the changes should help ensure there is no repeat in the future. Speaking to Dutch outlet Ziggo Sport last month, Lang said: "I still have it [my thumb] completely, that’s the most important thing.

"I just can't play PlayStation for a while, but that will come. Luckily, I only need my legs to be able to play football."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Seven players could miss Liverpool vs PSG as Curtis Jones injury update given READ MORE :

Premier League relegation picture as Spurs freefall and Leeds hold key with crunch games READ MORE :

After the game, Galatasaray filed an official complaint with UEFA and were considering a legal case for compensation. The club's general secretary Eray Yazgan told Turkish news outlet HTSport the day after the game: "After the match, we lodged a complaint with UEFA representatives regarding the matter. They conducted their investigation.

"UEFA will evaluate the issue. We are consulting with lawyers. We will submit our compensation claim to UEFA. We will request that our grievances regarding salaries be addressed. If our request is not met, a lawsuit may be filed. Our priority is the health of our players."

In a statement, Galatasaray club doctor Yener Ince explained more on the injury last month, saying: "I want to talk about the condition of our two players who were injured in the Champions League Round of 16 match against Liverpool.

‌



View 2 Images Galatasaray's Noa Lang is placed on a stretcher after a bad injury to his thumb (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

"Our player Noa Lang has suffered a serious injury to the first finger of his right hand. I want to clarify that there is no complete amputation; however, the injury is significant.

"Because this area needed urgent repair, he underwent a successful operation in Liverpool as quickly as possible, without being brought to Istanbul."

Sports.title: Man Utd set to launch Lisandro Martinez red card appeal after Michael Carrick comments
Sports.content:
Man Utd set to launch Lisandro Martinez red card appeal after Michael Carrick comments

Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez was sent off in the Red Devils’ defeat to Leeds at Old Trafford and club chiefs are set to launch a bid to see his ban overturned

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez is set to miss the next three games (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United will appeal Lisandro Martinez’s ‘shocking’ red card against Leeds. The Argentine defender was dismissed at Old Trafford on Monday evening for pulling Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s hair.

‌



Martinez now faces a three-match ban and could potentially miss upcoming games against Chelsea, Brentford and Liverpool.

‌



But United are determined to have the centre-back available for the run-in as they aim to secure a spot in the Champions League. As per The Telegraph, United will lodge an appeal in the hope that the red card gets overturned.

‌



One man who will be keen to see the ban cancelled is United boss Michael Carrick, who was left furious at the decision to send the defender off.

Speaking after his side’s defeat to Leeds, Carrick said: "It's not a pull, it's not a tug, it's not aggressive, he touches it and gets sent off. Worst of all is he was sent to overturn it as a clear and obvious error. It's shocking.

Man Utd squad get their way after claiming major decision was 'madness' READ MORE :

Gary Neville identifies Man Utd detail that gives biggest hint yet over manager decision READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated F acebook page

‌



"He's off-balance because of that, he half touches the back of his hair which pulls the bobble out and leads it to look like - I don't even know what it looks like. That's two games in a row we've had those decisions go against us, but that one was one of the worst I've seen."

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher gave his thoughts on the decision and claimed that Martinez should not have been dismissed.

He said: "He's going for the ball and he's almost grappling. He's trying to grab onto something and he's caught the back of his hair - it could've been his hair or anything," said the ex-Liverpool star.

‌



View 2 Images Martinez was sent off for pulling Calvert-Lewin's hair (Image: Getty Images)

"He's got him for about half a second. We hear from Howard Webb and he says 'what does the game want?'

"I don't think any football fan, manager or player is thinking 'that's a red card'. Everybody is looking at that and thinking 'oh come on, that is not a red card, behave yourself'."

‌



United icon Roy Keane also offered his verdict and suggested that he could see why Martinez was sent off despite the decision being ‘harsh’. He added: "I can see it from both sides and when you class it as violent conduct, it feels really harsh.

"But we've seen other players getting sent off. It is harsh but if that's the laws of the game, then you have to accept it."

Martinez, 28, has played 15 Premier League games for United this season, having been blighted by both knee and calf injuries throughout the campaign.

Sports.content:
Man Utd squad get their way after claiming major decision was 'madness'

A key Manchester United star saw his future resolved with his team-mates clamouring for him to remain at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Harry Maguire's future was clinched last week (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

The Manchester United squad have got their wish after Harry Maguire last week put pen to paper on a one-year extension to his contract. The bulk of the squad believed it would have been "madness" if the experienced defender hadn't been handed a fresh deal.

‌



The 33-year-old is back in favour having endured a tough spell under both Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. The centre-back, who arrived at United from Leicester City for £80million, has proved to be an influential leader under Michael Carrick's stewardship.

‌



Maguire has led by example for his colleagues and they were reportedly pushing hard for a new contract for the England international. A source told The Sun earlier this year: "The players think it would be madness if he was not offered a new deal.

‌



"Harry has endured plenty of ups and downs at United but has come through all that and is playing really well. He's very well-respected in the dressing room and is passing on a lot of knowledge to some of the younger players like Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro.

"Everyone likes him and respects him and the majority of the players want the club to give him a deal." Reports emerged that AC Milan had been keen on Maguire during the January transfer window.

Gary Neville identifies Man Utd detail that gives biggest hint yet over manager decision READ MORE :

Man Utd debate put to bed by PGMOL rule and Howard Webb after red card fury READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



However, speculation surrounding his future ultimately amounted to nothing as the seasoned defender penned a new deal with United last week. His previous contract had been due to expire at the end of this season but he will now embark on an eighth campaign at Old Trafford.

Speaking of his delight at the new agreement, Maguire said: "It's amazing. Obviously, it's my seventh year. To be at this club, to play for this club for one game is really special. So, to be here seven years - it's going to be eight - I'm really looking forward to it.

View 2 Images Harry Maguire signed a new contract last week (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



"A big, strong end to the season is the focus now, to put us in a strong position going into next year, and then we've got to make next year a lot better and a lot more positive and a lot more special. I'm really looking forward to it."

Maguire's new deal will be warmly welcomed by the senior dressing room, as the side look to secure a return to European football next season. United's revival under Carrick has been nothing short of remarkable for supporters, with the club firmly in contention for a Champions League berth.

Maguire believes the team have turned a corner and will make the 2026/27 season a "special year" for the club. He added: "I feel like we're in a good place at the moment. I believe we're in a forward curve with the club, and I want to be part of that.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Richarlison makes startling confession – 'I thought about crashing into a wall'
Sports.content:
Tottenham star Richarlison makes startling confession – 'I thought about crashing into a wall'

Tottenham Hotspur star Richarlison has discussed his mental health struggles

View 2 Images Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has spoken about his battle with depression (Image: Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur star Richarlison has admitted he considered crashing his car into a wall during a battle with depression. The forward was deeply affected by the pressure that surrounded him following Brazil’s exit at the World Cup 2022.

‌



From the outside, the World Cup was a positive experience for the 28-year-old, whose bicycle kick against Serbia won the goal of the tournament. The Spurs forward had been given the honour of leading the line for the five-time World Cup winners.

‌



He scored three goals in total but could not prevent his country from being eliminated by Croatia on penalties in the quarter-finals. However, the disappointment took a toll on his mental health and Richarlison has shared how his thoughts began to spiral.

‌



"One day, while driving, I thought about crashing into a wall,” Richarlison said to France Football. “Today, when I think about it, I tell myself it's pointless.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He continued: "After the 2022 World Cup, I fell into a depression. Every possible misfortune befell me: the elimination, my agent's betrayal, family problems, physical setbacks... For a year and a half, I suffered blow after blow every single day.”

‌



What every Tottenham star will earn if relegation clauses are triggered - with thousands lost READ MORE :

Premier League relegation picture as Spurs freefall and Leeds hold key with crunch games READ MORE :

Having signed for Spurs from Everton in the summer of 2022, the striker ended his first season with just one league goal. However, through working with a psychologist, Richarlison rediscovered a more positive mindset.

"It was the first time I had to deal with so many problems,” he explained. ”In all that chaos, I met an honest lawyer who put my affairs and assets in order. I worked with a psychologist and, most importantly, I met my wife."

As the World Cup 2026 approaches, the former Everton icon plans to take Manchester United midfielder Casemiro’s advice and not look at social media if he is named in Carlo Ancelotti’s squad. However, it is not the first time that Richarlison has given an insight into his struggles with depression.

‌



View 2 Images Richarlison struggled after Brazil were knocked out of the 2022 World Cup (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

In March 2024, during a heartfelt interview with ESPN Brasil, the Spurs striker said: “I was reaching my limit, you know? I don’t know, I’m not going to talk about killing myself, but I was in a depression there, and I wanted to give up.”

He added: “Today I can say, look for a psychologist, if you need a psychologist, look for one because it’s nice for you to open up like that, for you to be talking to the person.

‌



“Today a (psychologist) came to thank me for taking this to the world of football, to the world, outside the pitch too, because it is very important and, whether we like it or not, it saves lives.

“I had this prejudice before, I thought it was nonsense, I thought I was crazy. In my family, there are people who think that anyone who goes to a psychologist thinks they are crazy, they think they are insane. But I discovered this and thought it was wonderful. The best thing, really the best discovery I’ve ever had in my life.”

Richarlison has scored 10 goals in 38 appearances for Spurs this season. He most recently played for Brazil in October 2025.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has made his first serious error in audition for Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has made his first serious error in audition for Man Utd job

On-trial Manchester United manager was furious with referee Paul Tierney after the defeat to Leeds United at Old Trafford but he should have been blaming others closer to home

View 2 Images Michael Carrick came out with highly critical comments about the refereeing of his side's loss to Leeds United (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Without doubt, the Lisandro Martinez hair-pull was even less violent than the one which got Everton’s Michael Keane sent off against Wolves at Hill Dickinson Stadium back in January. But from the moment Keane’s ‘offence’ against Wolves’ Tolu Arokodare was deemed worthy of a straight red card - and a three-match suspension - it was clear Premier League referees had been given the word.

‌



Zero tolerance on hair-pulling. A yank, a tug, whatever, it doesn’t matter. And no matter how incredulous Michael Carrick and a legion of ex-professionals declared themselves to be, there will be no change in the policy. Certainly not this season.

‌



Pull hair, get sent off. And no matter how soft the dismissal of Martinez looked, you cannot accidentally pull someone’s hair.

‌



Whether this zero-tolerance approach will continue next season is another matter, but the problem referees will have is deciding when a hair-pull is soft enough for a yellow card or no punishment, and when it is hard enough for a red card. Far simpler to say: hey, just don’t pull someone’s hair.

Anyway, the point is that while the red card for Martinez did seem extremely harsh, it was not ‘absolutely shocking’. Once Paul Tierney believes the footage shows even the slightest pull, the Manchester United man is off.

Andoni Iraola to leave Bournemouth as Man Utd learn chances of landing new boss READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



What was shocking, though, was Carrick’s post-match reaction. It was his first serious mis-step in his extended audition for the long-term job.

That he was outraged by the decision was not shocking - a lot of people were equally outraged. I can safely say in the list of Martinez offences that have been deemed worthy of sanction since he has been in the Premier League, this was way down the scale.

But Carrick had just enjoyed the luxury of three weeks to prepare for a game against a team that had won just ONE Premier League away game all season. And that win was against a Wolves team at their most hapless early in the season.

‌



And don’t forget, Carrick has a squad assembled at a cost in excess of £800 million. The total outlay on Daniel Farke’s squad was just over £200million. Most pertinently of all, Leeds United were two goals to the good at the time of the Martinez offence and looked in relatively little danger.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez was stunned by Paul Tierney's decision to send him off for a hair-pull on Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Image: Getty Images)

You can easily understand the manager’s frustration. He is now going to be without Martinez for three games, although even before the red card, it would be fair to describe the Argentine’s comeback performance as mixed.

‌



But even if it was not his intention, Carrick’s broadside against the officials diverted attention away from the most unsatisfactory performance in what is essentially a trial period for the manager, and the message from Carrick should have been clear. He didn’t agree with the sending-off call but the real issue is that United players had lapsed into pre-Carrick levels of performance and that is something he will address.

Heading into the remaining six Premier League fixtures with a seven-point advantage over sixth-placed Chelsea (the top five qualify for the Champions League), Carrick is still in the box seat for the long-term role. But Monday night’s efforts - and the subsequent moaning about officials - were the sorts of things that could change executive opinion of Carrick very dramatically.

Sports.title: Why penalty decisions went against Man Utd at Bournemouth
Sports.content:
PGMO chief refereeing officer Howard Webb says the penalty decisions that went against Manchester United at Bournemouth were because of the difference in the "speed the attackers are moving at".

Man Utd led twice on the south coast in March through Bruno Fernandes and a James Hill own goal, but Ryan Christie and a late penalty from Eli Junior Kroupi earned the hosts a point in an incident-packed match.

Fernandes scored from the spot after a pull by Alex Jimenez on Matheus Cunha, but United winger Amad Diallo had a penalty appeal dismissed on-field and by the VAR during the second half when he went down after being held by Adrien Truffert, seconds before the hosts equalised.

Centre-back Harry Maguire was then shown a straight red card for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity after he pulled over Evanilson, giving away a penalty in the process which Kroupi scored from.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Christie pulls one back for Bournemouth after Amad Diallo was denied penalty in their Premier League clash with Manchester United

Match Officials Mic'd Up revealed assistant referee Constantine Hatzidakis didn't see the Amad incident as he was "looking at the line" with referee Stuart Attwell believing the winger was "waiting for the contact". VAR Craig Pawson said the contact was "not sufficient for how he goes down" but he saw the Maguire foul as "a cynical hold across".

Webb said: "They're both pushing actions, but there are some differences. Most of the difference sits around the speed the attackers are moving at.

"In Amad's case, he wasn't moving particularly quickly. There was some contact. It's a judgment call on how impactful it is.

"Evanilson is going past Maguire. It's a completely different pace, in my opinion, to Amad. Maguire desperately pushes him over to stop him from going through to score. A very clear situation of a foul.

"The on-field decision was foul. In both cases, the referee's decision was respected by the VAR and the referee's call stood.

"In this situation [Maguire foul], if the referee hadn't given a penalty, then I think VAR would have stepped in because, in my opinion, it's clearly and obviously a penalty."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Maguire is sent off for pulling Evanilson and Eli Junior Kroupi converts the penalty to bring Bournemouth level in their Premier League clash with Manchester United

Fernandes was furious that only one of the penalties was awarded for "the same situation" while head coach Michael Carrick said it was "crazy" and "baffling" not to give both.

Webb added: "Truffert takes a risk. He places his hands on Amad, who is not moving at a great pace, but he is moving and there is definitely contact.

"We know that players come into contact quite often, particularly in and around the penalty area. The referee has to make a judgment on how impactful that action is.

"The referee deemed it wasn't sufficient to award a penalty. The referee's call is an important part of the way we apply VAR. Time and time again, people tell us not to be too intrusive, only step in when something is really clearly wrong.

"In this situation, the VAR deemed it was a subjective call - could be a penalty, but it's one of those grey situations. The Key Match Incident panel agreed with that. They were split a little bit, but they agreed on balance, it wasn't a clear penalty and supported the on-field decision."

Carrick: We should have had another penalty

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes questioned the decision to deny Manchester United a penalty for a push on Amad Diallo before awarding Bournemouth a penalty for a seemingly similar situation with Harry Maguire and Evanilson

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to Sky Sports after the 2-2 draw:

"We should have had another penalty. Obviously, if you get one, you must get the other.

"It's pretty much identical for me, two-hand grab. Either way, he's got one wrong, but to give one and not give the other, I can't get my head around it, I think it's crazy. It's a bit baffling, really.

"Because of that, they score and then it's chaos after that, really. We should have had another penalty and the game would have been totally different."

Sports.title: 'Definitely not unfair!' - McIlroy's crucial Masters preparation at Augusta defended
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy's preparations for his successful Masters defence have come under scrutiny, but questions over the fairness of his time spent at Augusta National have been firmly dismissed.

McIlroy became just the fourth player to win back-to-back Masters after holding on to beat Scottie Scheffler by one shot on Sunday.

Having completed a career Grand Slam by winning at Augusta in 2025, McIlroy claiming the sixth major title of his career 12 months later has further elevated the Northern Irishman's standing among the sport's all-time greats.

Despite there being no doubt over McIlroy's excellence, comments he made midway through the event, revealing the regularity with which he had played at Augusta in recent weeks, have led to a post-tournament debate.

One of America's leading sports talk shows debated on Monday whether McIlroy had gained an unfair advantage by playing at Augusta, leading several others to weigh in on the debate on social media.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his successful title defence at The Masters, McIlroy reflects on his triumph and talks 'potential' for more success

'I've been on this golf course so much'

McIlroy made a stunning start to his title defence by reaching 12 under at the halfway stage, opening up a record six-shot lead over the rest of the field.

Speaking after his second round, McIlroy explained how he thought he had been aided by using the weeks ahead of the tournament to practice at Augusta, as he skipped all three PGA Tour events between The Players and The Masters.

McIlroy said: "I've been on this golf course so much the last three weeks, and that's been a combination of practice and chipping and putting around greens, and then just playing one ball and shooting scores and ending up in weird places that you maybe never find yourself and just trying to figure it out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy posted a stunning seven-under-par 65 at Augusta National to hold a record 36-hole lead at The Masters!

"I think just spending so much time up here has been a big part of it.

"I honestly just don't like the three tournaments leading up to this event.

"I'd rather come up here. I did a couple of days where I dropped [my daughter] Poppy to school, flew up here, played, landed back home and had dinner with her, or had dinner with [my wife] Erica.

"I did a couple of day trips like that where I felt it was a better use of my time than going to Houston or San Antonio. It wasn't really about conserving energy, but just I felt the more time I could spend up here, the better."

'An advantage, but not an unfair one'

McIlroy's quotes received immediate attention on social media, but questions over the fairness of his build-up to the tournament were put on hold when he gave up his six-shot lead during the third round.

However, once McIlroy had produced a spirited display on Sunday, coming from behind to win, some returned their focus to the time he had spent at Augusta ahead of the tournament.

The segment on US television sparked a debate, in which the golfing community has emphatically defended McIlroy. American duo Michael Kim and Kevin Kisner were among those to dismiss any questions over the champion's approach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy revealed how he ranked each part of his golf game during the 2026 Masters

Sky Sports Golf's Nick Dougherty said: "It has no sense to it really. I feel like that's more the people outside of golf not really understanding the process, how it all works and what's available to the players, probably driving it.

"It's probably testament to the fact that the Masters is a sports event that grabs the attention rather than just a golf one.

"It's definitely not an unfair advantage. You earn that right to be able to go there."

After finishing in a tie for 46th as he failed to defend his Players title early in March, McIlroy then chose not to play in the Valspar Championship, Houston Open and Texas Open, which filled the three weeks before The Masters.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy played Amen Corner in two-under par to pull clear of the chasing pack and take a firm grip of The Masters during Sunday's final round at Augusta National

Dougherty continued: "Was it an advantage that he did it? Yes, but it's not an unfair one. It's smart. And his unfair advantage is he's so good he doesn't need to go and play all these tournaments beforehand. But again, he's earned that, hasn't he?

"Rory McIlroy can play a limited schedule because he knows that when he does play, he's probably going to make them count. And he's earned the chance to play when he wants to play now. He doesn't have to turn up just because it's a big event at a golf course.

"Whereas the lesser players, as you're building your way up, you play a lot more golf and you play where you can. But of course, that's not where he is because of all the things he's achieved."

'Rory didn't get anything anyone else wouldn't have got'

Dougherty made the only Masters appearance of his career in 2008, and insists the treatment he received from Augusta officials suggests other entrants to the 2026 tournament could have practiced on the course just as often as McIlroy if they had wanted to do so.

"I came seventh in the 2007 US Open, so I knew from June of 2007 that in April of 2008, I was going to be playing in the Masters," Dougherty recalled.

Image: Sky Sports Golf's Nick Dougherty made his sole Masters appearance in 2008

"And so when the opportunity arose, Sir Nick Faldo gave me the advice to make sure I went early because if you just turn up on the tournament week, the wow factor, certainly as a first-timer, is just going to blow you away and it's going to really affect your performance. You need to go and do your homework and take the time, to do exactly what Rory actually did.

"They gave me a brilliant caddie from Augusta National who showed me all the nuances - you're not going to get that on tournament week because you have your own caddie - and we spent ages on the course.

"There are obviously not a lot of people there when you go. The club are really forthcoming in allowing you to properly practice while you're out there on the golf course, hit all different shots, all different pin positions. And so even though it was the first time I knew the place like the back of my hand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy spoke prior to his second round of The Masters where he revealed the advice Jack Nicklaus gave him

"Sure, they're going to be probably slightly more helpful with Rory, but I still think he's probably only gone the amount that someone probably could have called up as a first timer to go and play and see the golf course. I doubt he went more than five times or something.

"I'm pretty sure the golf club would look after someone wanting to practice and prepare for the Masters if they went through the right protocol of calling up. So, I don't honestly think that he got anything anyone else wouldn't have done.

"People just think it's unfair because they assume you can't go there, and because it's Rory, they're saying, 'ok, you can.' That's not how it is."

Doherty was backed up by current World No 44 Michael Kim, who said he had "plenty of chances" to play Augusta ahead of this year's tournament.

Kim wrote on social media: "Yes, there is a number of rounds that ANGC will say no to for me to go by myself and play by myself. That number is prob a little lower for me than a guy like Rory.

"If you find a member to host you every time, there's no limit. "I had plenty of chances to go to ANGC myself if I wanted to but didn't go. Better use of my time practicing at home or wherever I am to get my game in better shape for my next tournament.

"If I wanted to match the number of rounds at Augusta that Rory got, I easily could have done that."
